Question Choices: Select. A reflection maps figure P onto figure Q exactly. Are P and Q congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A reflection is a rigid motion.|Rigid motions preserve size and shape.
Solution: Translations, rotations and reflections are rigid motions: they preserve size and shape. Mapping one complete figure exactly onto the other by a rigid motion or a sequence of them establishes congruence.

Question Choices: Select. Two segments have lengths 8 and 8. Are they congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Segments are congruent when lengths match.|Both are 8.
Solution: Yes. Both segments have length 8 in the same units. Equal segment lengths are exactly the condition for segment congruence.

Question Choices: Select. Two angles measure 30 degrees and 60 degrees. Are they congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Solution: No. Congruent angles must have equal measures, but 30 degrees is not 60 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. A dilation with scale factor 1 maps one figure to another. Are they congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A factor of 1 leaves lengths unchanged.|The image equals the original in size.
Solution: Yes. A factor-1 dilation fixes every point, so it is the identity. All corresponding lengths and angles match.

Question Choices: Which transformations preserve both distance and angle measure: rigid motions or dilations with factor 2?
Hints: Compare a nonzero distance before and after each transformation.|Rigid motions preserve distances and angles; factor-2 dilations double lengths.
Solution: Rigid motions preserve both distance and angle measure. A dilation with factor 2 preserves angles but doubles distances, so it does not preserve both.
